github_issue.notes: The issue pins the problem (no external policy hook between permission checks and persistence), commits to exact semantics (200 allow, 403 deny with surfaced reason, fail-closed on timeout/unreachable/non-200/403), and lists all seven gated routes which I verified against the repo (agent_routes.py:330 register/1195 update, server_routes.py:627/852/2436, skill_routes.py:611/660), plus real out-of-scope boundaries (edit/toggle/delete/federation, retries, caching, async approval) with rationale. The httpx dependency claim is verified in pyproject.toml:19. Largest deficiencies: one acceptance criterion hedges the fail-closed status ('502/503-family or 403 per LLD') instead of committing, the 'no secrets leaked' criterion is only loosely testable, and the referenced issue #809 and repo labels are unverifiable offline; the gate-outage blast radius on automated internal registrations is left to the LLD rather than stated here.

lld.notes: This is the strongest artifact: essentially every load-bearing claim checks out against the source, including exact route line numbers (server_routes.py:627/852/2436), AgentRegistrationRequest at agent_models.py:818 and SkillRegistrationRequest at skill_models.py:285, the module-singleton settings constraint (tests/conftest.py:277 mock_settings), the form-data (not JSON) shape of server routes, and the ans_client.py per-call httpx pattern. It commits to the decisions that matter: fail-closed 403/503 mapping, auth_credential redaction, URL scheme validation, timeout floor, and a per-call-site payload/user table naming real symbols; the deployment checklist covers surfaces I confirmed exist (terraform root/module/main.tf, Helm secret consumed via envFrom in deployment.yaml:48). The main defect is an internal contradiction on test seams — 'Existing Patterns' correctly says to patch registry.api.registration_gate.check_registration_gate for the lazy function-local import, while the Testing Strategy summary says 'patched at the route-module import seam' — which is the seed of the broken route tests in the implementation; the mcpgw/overwrite blast-radius note is asserted but its caller behavior is not verifiable in-repo.

review.notes: This is a real review, not role-play: Byte's must-fix on auth_credential leakage is grounded in the actual Form() signatures (server_routes.py:642/866/2451), Circuit's catch that root terraform/aws-ecs/main.tf wiring was missing is a genuine Terraform requirement I verified (module inputs only reachable via main.tf:124-style wiring), and Cipher's scheme-validation/timeout-floor/redaction items are concrete with folded-back resolutions and a prioritized summary table. It disagrees with the draft in actionable ways and the next-steps section maps each fix to an LLD change. The gap: Sage's test-seam resolution (#8) claims testing.md states per-layer patch targets, but testing.md's own code examples contradict its seam map and the review did not catch that contradiction, nor the router-prefix mounting issue that later breaks the implementation's route tests; all verdicts are APPROVED WITH CHANGES with no dissent, which is defensible here since the findings are non-architectural.

testing.notes: The plan targets the right levels with real oracles: exact envelope JSON equality, exact denial-reason strings per response key, assert_not_called for disabled/misconfigured gates, a redaction assertion that checks the raw secret never appears, default-off settings assertions, deployment greps against files that exist, and a rollback check. The seam map correctly prescribes patching registry.api.registration_gate.check_registration_gate for route tests, matching the lazy import design. The largest defect is that its own route-level examples (section 1.2 and the redaction test) use the wrong target registry.api.agent_routes.check_registration_gate — which raises AttributeError given the function-local import — and none of the examples address router mounting (existing tests use registry.main.app for server/skill routes and unprefixed /agents/register for the bare agent router), so following the plan verbatim yields errors and 404s; the disabled-gate case is also only covered at unit level plus a hand-waved representative route, versus the issue's 'for each gated route'.

implementation.notes: The production half of the patch is excellent and verified against the source: all 14 hunks' context matches the checkout line-for-line (agent_routes.py:372/1245, server_routes.py:669/887/2535, skill_routes.py:634/700, config.py:120, plus exact .env.example/compose/terraform/Helm anchors), all seven gate calls sit after permission/ownership checks and before persistence with real symbols, credentials are redacted in all three server payloads, and the TF auth header is marked sensitive. The largest defect is the 641-line test file: every route-wiring test patches registry.api.<routes>.check_registration_gate, which raises AttributeError because the implementation imports the gate function-locally inside handlers, and the test apps mount the routers without the /api prefix while posting /api/... paths (existing tests use registry.main.app or unprefixed /agents/register), so those tests cannot pass as written — contradicting the summary's 'runnable' claim; test_gate_allow_returns_none_and_sends_envelope also asserts call_args.kwargs['url'] though the implementation passes the URL positionally (KeyError). The summary is otherwise honest (deviations, follow-ups, tests not executed), and the allow-proceeds tests use the weak oracle 'not in (403, 503)'.

verdict: A well-grounded, internally consistent design set with a production patch whose source and deployment changes verify cleanly against the repository, limited most materially by a route-wiring test suite that cannot pass as written (wrong patch seam for the lazy gate import and missing /api router prefix) despite being presented as runnable.
